title: The neurons the loop finds are about the concept, not the question wording
detail: Top-5 neurons (found on Luna's questions) zeroed on independent Wikipedia cloze prompts: median drop +5.59 log-odds vs -0.003 for 5 random same-layer neurons; flips at least half the correct prompts in 66% of concepts (32 tested).

title: 'Dedicated' neurons fall predictably as more concepts are mapped
detail: Predicted 29.4% of neurons firing for no other concept at N = 609 comparison concepts; observed 32.0% (limit +-3 points).

title: When two concepts share a neuron, it matters causally to both
detail: 150 pairs sharing exactly one top-10 neuron: zeroing it drops B by a median +0.835 log-odds (A: +0.894) vs +0.002 for A's non-shared neuron and +0.000 for a random one.

title: The map's structure predicts the neurons of concepts it has not seen
detail: Family neurons (Wikidata 'instance of') appear in 191 new concepts' top-30 at 9.2x the other-family rate (needs 3x; p = 0.0001); 2,000 label shuffles never reach it. Caveat: family ~ type of answer word.

title: Where a neuron fires in web text is a stable, describable property
detail: Profiles on 2M new FineWeb tokens vs the atlas's 10M: Spearman 0.986 for firing rate, 0.883 for on-concept share.

title: Confirmatory replication on 40 never-used concepts
detail: 40/40 recalled, 0/4 made-up; <= 5 neurons for 98%; answers flip with <= 5 neurons for 85%; the most resistant facts are the most confident (p = 0.005); per-concept steering 2.44x the fixed rule. Failed: people steerable but less than other concepts.

title: About half of neurons verifiably do one job
detail: Calibrated census of 1,000 random neurons (954 live): ~50% of positive and ~47% of negative poles pass a bar that passes only 8% / 4% of known two-job dossiers. Closer to a floor than an estimate. The essay reports ~90% for Qwen3-32B.
